examples.input: Summarize the following incident report in 2 sentences: On Nov 24 at 03:12 UTC, the auth-proxy service experienced a 14-minute elevated 502 rate due to an expired TLS leaf certificate on the upstream token-signer. Rotating the cert via Vault restored normal traffic by 03:26 UTC.
examples.expected: An expired TLS leaf certificate on the token-signer caused a 14-minute 502 spike in auth-proxy on Nov 24. Rotating the certificate via Vault resolved the outage at 03:26 UTC.
examples.output: On Nov 24 at 03:12 UTC, auth-proxy suffered 14 minutes of elevated 502 errors caused by an expired TLS leaf certificate on the upstream token-signer. Service was restored at 03:26 UTC after rotating the certificate in Vault.

examples.input: Write a TypeScript function `chunkArray<T>(arr: T[], size: number): T[][]` that splits an array into chunks of at most `size` elements. Throw an Error if `size <= 0`.
examples.expected: Throws if size <= 0, slices array in steps of size.

examples.input: Extract name, role, and start_date as JSON from: 'Priya Nair joined as Staff Security Engineer on 2026-09-15.'

If a rate limiter allows 15 requests per minute with a sliding window, and a client sends 10 requests at t=0s and 5 requests at t=40s, when is the earliest time the client can send 1 more request without being rate-limited?
examples.expected: t=60s (when the 10 requests from t=0s fall outside the 60s window).
examples.output: At t=40s, the client has used all 15 requests in the [0s, 60s] window. The earliest requests (10 of them at t=0s) expire at t=60s, so the client can send 1 more request at t=60s.
